70,000 Rural Youth to Begin Skill Training Under DDU-GKY 2.0 Across States/UTs from October 2026
articles.full_content:
Ministry of Rural Development Accelerates DDU-GKY 2.0 Rollout Across States/UTs
The Ministry of Rural Development is set to roll out Deen Dayal Upadhyaya- Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 2.0 training batches across most of the States/UTs from October 2026.
As per the DDU-GKY 2.0 portal ( https://kaushal.rural.gov.in ) allocations of 5.6 lakh targets towards more than 1,200 projects to the Project Implementation Agencies (PIAs) have been done by 24 States/UTs. Other States are in the advanced stages of target allocations. Across the country in 24 States/UTs, 2,015 batches involving around 70,000 rural youth are expected to commence their training in October 2026.
DDU-GKY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme providing placement linked skill training to poor rural youth. Duration of the training varies from 3 months to 12 months. All the 31 participating States/UTs have been allocated more than 9 lakhs targets under the DDU-GKY 2.0 for 2-year period 2026-28. States/UTs have to mobilise rural youth and to organise placement linked skill training, as per demand, in PPP mode, in National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) aligned courses, enabling sustained employability of the beneficiaries. The Ministry emphasised that this is a crucial phase for State/UT action and called upon implementing States/UTs to accelerate the allocation of targets to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) and to commence batches as per envisaged timelines. States/UTs are supposed to ensure allocation of targets to PIAs for commencement of trainings latest by 31 October 2026.
Review meetings in phases are being held with the States/UTs to gather momentum in the processes leading to batch commencements.

articles.full_content:
Shri C. R. Patil Calls for Collective Action to Strengthen Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Water Management at IIWW 2026 IIWW 2026 Brings Together Global Water Community to Advance Innovation, Knowledge and Sustainable WASH Solutions India International WASH Conference Highlights Community-Led Approaches, Digital Innovation and Stronger Institutions for Sustainable Water Services
The 9 th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, with the Valedictory Ceremony chaired by Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil. Held from September 22–25 under the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management”, the deliberations brought together policymakers, government officials, international organisations, development partners, researchers, academia, industry, water-sector practitioners, innovators and young professionals to discuss emerging challenges and solutions for water security.
The valedictory session was graced by Ministers of State for Jal Shakti; Shri V. Somanna, Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Smt. Archana Varma, Director General, National Mission for Clean Ganga, Shri Rajeev Kumar Mital, AS & MD, NJJM, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and Director General, National Water Development Agency, Shri Baleshwar Thakur.
Addressing the gathering, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti underscored that IIWW 2026 provided a platform for governments, experts, institutions, academia, industry and youth to deliberate on climate-resilient water management. He highlighted three key takeaways: people’s participation in water conservation, taking science and technology to the ground, and strengthening international and institutional cooperation. Highlighting the Jal Jeevan Mission’s impact since its launch in 2019, he said expanded access to household tap water has contributed to improved health, dignity and quality of life in rural communities, while reducing the time and effort spent by women in fetching water. Referring to a WHO assessment, he said that improved access to safe drinking water under the Mission has the potential to prevent a significant number of deaths among children and reduce the health burden associated with unsafe water. He stressed that the next phase of JJM must focus on ensuring adequate, regular, safe and sustainable drinking water services, with community participation, source sustainability and appropriate technology central to sustaining these gains.

Ministry of New & Renewable Energy Gears Up for Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Ministry and its CPSUs and Autonomous Institutes Undertake Activities for Institutionalising Swachhata and Minimising Pendency
The preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6 is underway in the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE). Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimising pendency in Government offices. It is being implemented in the ministry along with its two CPSUs and three Autonomous Institutes.
The CPSUs include Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd. (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI), and Autonomous Institutes include National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) and Sardar Swarn Singh National Institute of Bio Energy (SSS-NIBE).
The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 will commence from 2nd October, 2026, during which concerted efforts will be made to achieve the targets identified during the Preparatory Phase and further institutionalise Swachhata, efficient record management and timely disposal of pendency across the Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions.
During the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6, the following activities are being undertaken by the Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions:
i. Identification and disposal of pendency under various parameters.
ii. Review, categorisation and weeding out of physical records as per extant guidelines.
iii. Conduct of cleanliness campaigns for maintaining cleanliness in the Ministry and its PSUs and Autonomous Institutes.
iv. Identification and segregation of e-waste as per MoEFCC guidelines for target setting during the Implementation Phase.
The Ministry and its PSUs/Institutions actively participated in Special Campaign 5 last year, with substantial progress recorded across key areas, including Public Grievances, Public Grievance Appeals, review of physical files and e-files, and cleanliness campaigns. During the Campaign, 725 targeted e-files were reviewed, while significant progress was also made in the disposal of references received from Members of Parliament. Further, 8 out of 9 targeted cleanliness campaigns were conducted, contributing to a cleaner and more productive workplace.
The Preparatory Phase of #SpecialCampaign6 is underway at the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its 2 PSUs—IREDA & SECI—and 3 Autonomous Institutes—NISE, NIWE & SSS-NIBE, as part of the Government’s continued efforts to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in Government offices. The Implementation Phase will be undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026. This year, the campaign places special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, along with cleanliness drives and the timely disposal of pending matters. Shillong Vartalap Highlights Public Awareness and Coordinated Action on Solid Waste Management Rules 2026
articles.full_content:
Dr Ampareen Lyngdoh Calls for Clear Communication and Coordinated Action for Effective Implementation
Greater public awareness, sustained media outreach and coordinated action among government agencies, Urban Local Bodies, Pollution Control Boards and citizens were emphasised for effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. Speaking at a Vartalap – Media Workshop held in Shillong in the spirit of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, Dr. Mazel Ampareen Lyngdoh, Member of Legislative Assembly from 16-East Shillong and Adviser to the Government of Meghalaya, called for clear and accessible communication of the Rules to strengthen public understanding and participation.
Organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Shillong, in coordination with the Urban Affairs Department, Government of Meghalaya, the Vartalap brought together government officials, technical agencies, Urban Local Bodies and the media to discuss the new Rules, implementation timelines and ways to communicate their provisions effectively to the public.
The Vartalap was held as part of the nationwide advocacy campaign for dissemination of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has extended support to the campaign and is working with the Urban Affairs Department and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on an appropriate media and dissemination strategy.
Appreciating the initiative, Dr. Lyngdoh commended PIB Shillong for bringing government departments, Urban Local Bodies, technical agencies and the media together on a common platform to discuss an issue of direct public importance. She also appreciated the Urban Affairs Department for its coordination and continued efforts to strengthen waste-management systems in the State.
She emphasised the need for officials to have a clear understanding of their responsibilities and communicate technical provisions in a manner that is accessible to communities. She also called for greater orientation of legislators and elected representatives on the new Rules, enabling them to engage effectively with the administration and the public. The media, she said, can play an important role in keeping citizens informed about implementation, challenges and measures being undertaken.
Reflecting on Meghalaya’s progress since 2014, Dr. Lyngdoh recalled that the State did not have a Project Management Unit (PMU) for urban sanitation at the time and communities largely relied on indigenous practices to address waste-related issues. She appreciated the Urban Affairs Department, PMU, Urban Local Bodies and municipal engineers for taking forward initiatives relating to waste management, sewage treatment and rainwater management.
Shri P. K. Boro, Director, Urban Affairs Department, Government of Meghalaya, outlined the State’s approach to urban waste management and initiatives being undertaken by the Department and Urban Local Bodies.

Minister of State for Power and New and Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Naik holds Bilateral Meeting with European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Delegation
articles.full_content:
Shri Shripad Naik, the Minister of State for Power and New and Renewable Energy, held a bilateral meeting with a delegation of the European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE), in New Delhi, on 24 September 2026. The meeting was held to review and further strengthen the ongoing cooperation between India and the European Union in the power sector.
The discussions covered a wide range of areas, including energy security, power sector transformation, low-carbon development, nuclear energy, carbon markets and development of new technologies. Both sides exchanged views on ongoing initiatives and explored avenues to deepen collaboration, building on the strong momentum in India-EU relations, including the significant progress achieved in the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.
Shri Shripad Naik highlighted India’s rapidly transforming power sector and the country’s efforts to build a resilient, reliable and future-ready energy system. He noted India’s progress in expanding non-fossil fuel capacity, including achieving the NDC commitments in this regard much ahead of the target, strengthening transmission and distribution infrastructure, deploying energy storage and smart-grid solutions, and advancing nuclear energy, energy efficiency and green hydrogen.
Both sides discussed opportunities for enhanced cooperation in emerging areas, including long-duration energy storage, digital power-system technologies, green hydrogen, carbon capture, utilization and storage, and nuclear technologies, including Small Modular Reactors. They also exchanged perspectives on carbon markets and the evolving carbon-pricing landscape, including Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).
The meeting reaffirmed the importance of energy and power cooperation as a key pillar of the India-EU partnership. Both sides expressed their commitment to continued engagement, exchange of expertise and deeper technological and institutional cooperation to support secure, resilient and sustainable energy systems.

The meeting was held to review and further strengthen the ongoing cooperation between India and the European Union in the power sector. The discussions covered a wide range of areas, including energy security, power sector transformation, low-carbon development, nuclear energy, carbon markets and development of new technologies.

articles.full_content:
India’s Journey towards a Manufacturing Nation
As Make in India completes twelve years, the initiative has transformed India’s manufacturing landscape by expanding production, investment and capabilities across industries. During this period, production has increased across electronics, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, steel, railways and defence. India has also developed the capacity to manufacture components, machinery, strategic materials and advanced technologies. Initiatives such as NSWS, PLI, PM GatiShakti and the India Industrial Land Bank have supported investment and production. New schemes focus on semiconductors, mobile phones, industrial parks, specialty steel and rare-earth magnets, further strengthening domestic manufacturing.
A New Direction for Indian Manufacturing
Twelve years ago, on 25 September 2014 , ‘ Make in India’ was launched with the ambition of becoming a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation.
The initiative focused on facilitating investment, fostering innovation and developing world-class infrastructure. Guided by ‘ Minimum Government, Maximum Governance’ , it has also sought to modernise processes and policies.
Over the years, Make in India has opened new opportunities for businesses and investors to participate in India’s manufacturing journey. The initiative has subsequently been expanded under Make in India 2.0 . The initiative now focuses on 27 sectors, which include 15 in manufacturing and 12 in services .
India’s Manufacturing at a Larger Scale
Manufacturing has recorded strong growth over time. Recent indicators also point to continued growth in manufacturing.
Manufacturing Gross Value Added (GVA) at constant prices recorded a compound annual growth rate of 10.88% between 2022-23 and 2025-26 under the revised national accounts series.
Industrial output provides another indication of recent growth. The manufacturing component of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) increased by 7.0% during April-July 2026 compared with the corresponding period of 2025.
Rising Production Across Key Manufacturing Industries
The expansion in manufacturing is also visible across several industries, with substantial increases in production and capacity.
• Electronics production increased nearly sevenfold, from ~₹1.9 lakh crore in 2014-15 to ~₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025-26 .
• Within this total, mobile-phone production rose approximately 33-fold , from ~₹18,000 crore to ~₹6.27 lakh crore over the same period. India is the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer by volume.
• Overall electronics production also recorded 15.8% growth in 2025–26 over the previous year.
• Vehicle production reached 31.03 million units in 2024-25 , ~33% higher than in 2014-15 .
• Several vehicle segments also recorded significantly higher production in 2024-25 compared with 2020-21 :
• Passenger and commercial vehicle production increased by 65% each .
• Three-wheeler production rose by 71% .
• Two-wheeler production grew by 30% .

During this period, production has increased across electronics, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, steel, railways and defence. India has also developed the capacity to manufacture components, machinery, strategic materials and advanced technologies.

Climate Resilience, Water Finance and Innovation in Focus on Day 3 of India International Water Week 2026
articles.full_content:
Deliberations span climate risk assessment, early warning systems, glacial lake monitoring, water-use efficiency and innovative financing India-Netherlands cooperation advances through two tripartite MoUs
The third day carried the 9 th India International Water Week 2026 deeper into its technical programme, into the forward-looking questions of climate risk, early warning, glacial lake monitoring, water pricing and the financing of resilient water infrastructure. Sessions ran in parallel across the Water Leaders' Forum, Country Forum, Practitioners' Forum, Thematic Forum and Start-Up Forum. The Thematic Forum closed the third of its seven sub-themes and moved through the fourth and fifth.
The day also widened the Week's international reach. The Start-Up Forum gave startups, MSMEs and academia a platform to pitch problem-driven water solutions. On the sidelines, a bilateral meeting advanced India-Netherlands cooperation, with two tripartite MoUs signed.
India-Netherlands Bilateral Meeting
On the sidelines of the 9 th India International Water Week-2026, a bilateral meeting between the Shri C R Patil, Minister of Jal Shakti and H.E. Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice Minister for Infrastructure and Water Management, Netherlands, was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Minister of State, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Shri Ishwarsinh Patel, Minister of State for Water Resources and Water Supply (Independent Charge), joined the meeting, along with H. E Marissa Gerard, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to India.
During the event, a tripartite MoU was signed between Central Water Commission, Kalpasar, Deptt. Govt. of Gujarat and Deltares, Netherlands for technical support. Another tripartite MoU was signed between CWC, Kalpasar Deptt. of Govt. of Gujarat and TU Delft Netherlands for capacity building and trainings. The MoUs will facilitate technical collaboration through sharing of Dutch expertise and advanced engineering practices for the planning, design and implementation of the project.
Country Forum (CF)
CF-4 on Private Capital Mobilisation in the Water Sector, convened with the World Bank, was chaired by Shri Baldeo Purushartha, Joint Secretary, DEA, GOI and co-chaired by Smt. Roshika Singh, Principal Country Officer, IFC India. The session opened with a keynote by Shri Saroj Kumar Jha, Global Water Director, World Bank, and was moderated by Mr. William Rex, Practice Manager for Water, World Bank, with Jain Irrigations, IFC India, Coca-Cola,VA Tech Wabag, Tata Capital, the Maharashtra Institution for Transformation (MITRA) and the Uttar Pradesh State Transformation Commission, on the reforms and financing mechanisms needed to unlock private investment in urban water, wastewater and irrigation.

Two-Day Training on “Plant Identification, Herbarium Techniques and Impact of Climate Change at High Altitudes Using Different Ecological Tools" Begins at BSI, Gangtok
articles.full_content:
Gangtok, 24th September 2026
A two-day training programme on “Plant Identification, Herbarium Techniques and Impact of Climate Change at High Altitudes Using Different Ecological Tools” commenced today at the Sikkim Himalayan Regional Centre (SHRC) of the Botanical Survey of India (BSI), Gangtok.
Organised by BSI, SHRC under the NMHS project “Assessment of Floristic Diversity in the Alpine High Altitude Wetland Complexes of Sikkim” in collaboration with G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment (GBPNIHE), the programme aims to strengthen skills in plant identification, herbarium techniques and ecological assessment of climate change impacts on fragile high-altitude ecosystems.
In his welcome address, Dr. Rajib Gogoi, Scientist-F & Head of Office, BSI, SHRC, traced BSI’s legacy from its origins as the Calcutta Garden to its present role as the apex body for documentation of wild plants. He said the Sikkim Centre, established in 1979, houses 56,000 herbarium specimens of 5,149 species and 700 live plant species, and has brought out major publications including the pictorial Flora of Sikkim and contributed four volumes to the Flora of India.
Dr. Niladri Bag, Professor, Sikkim University, said Sikkim is a living laboratory of plant diversity. Noting that extinction rates are 1,000 to 10,000 times higher than natural rates, he stressed the need to attract students to taxonomy, which provides the foundation for ecology, conservation, agriculture and medicine.
Shri N. Jaswant Singh, IFS, Conservator of Forests, Sikkim, emphasised integration of scientific knowledge with forestry and suggested BSI-Forest Department collaboration in herbarium development and wildlife corridor identification.
Shri Rajesh Joshi, Regional Head, GBPNIHE, highlighted the need for accurate documentation and trained human resources to address climate change and developmental pressures in the Eastern Himalayas through a multidisciplinary approach.
Dr. T. N. Deka, ICRI, Spices Board, underlined the importance of correct identification of medicinal and economically important plants for healthcare, agriculture and preparedness in high-altitude terrains. Dr. S. S Bora of Spices Board was also present on this occasion.
Shri Manas Pratim Sarma, Assistant Director, Akashvani News and PIB, Gangtok also addressed the programme.
The programme also featured various technical sessions and activity conducted by various experts including Dr. Rajib Gogoi, Dr. Geetamani Chhetri, Dr. U.L. Tiwari, Shri Sabuj Barman, Shri Norbu Sherpa and Shri Palzor T. Lepcha.
The training is being attended by students, researchers and faculty from various institutions
